payload.title: Nonlinear candidate coverage and visible-prefix selector regret
payload.statement: A legal bank of genuinely different whole-well nonlinear paths can achieve candidate-oracle RMSE below 5, and multi-cut visible-prefix evidence plus calibrated uncertainty can retain enough of that coverage without hidden-label routing.
payload.evidence_for: The 773-well oracle smooth curve reaches 3.1106 while the oracle line stalls at 6.6972. Amer reports complementary PF/HMM sample errors, and Pilkwang exposes PF, beam, DTW, self-correlation, projection and uncertainty candidates.
payload.evidence_against: The fixed PF/beam selector scores 10.5831 and concentrates 61.95% of SSE in its worst decile. Repeated GR motifs, missingness, faults, and prefix-to-suffix distribution shift may make legal selection impossible even when oracle coverage is strong.
payload.next_test: E010: freeze a legal candidate bank, calculate oracle coverage under all maps, then train/evaluate only visible-prefix multi-cut selector probabilities and regret. Preserve E006 fallback and require repeated, tail, shift, control, runtime and parity gates.
